reviews.title: Service newly degraded over VPN
reviews.text:
Boo-Hiss on the latest version of the Bloomberg Prifessional app: 6.67.0.  

The new app often won't load stories when one clicks into them, bleating about a "network error" as its excuse, but really because the service is being accessed through a VPN.

Bloomberg is the only news source I pay for and I expect for my money to not be tracked in what I read. 

Previous versions of the Bloomberg app only forced one to choose whether to accept or reject cookies.  When one chooses to reject said cookies the old versions attempted to force "your cookie choices" down one's throat with each new session. 

This was an acceptable detante as one had an opportunity to tell the overly gropey Bloomberg app developers where to shove it each and every day.

This new version is far worse and far from being a game-changer is in fact a game-ender.

reviews.title: Beware: My Bloomberg Digital renewal jumped from $149 to $399 — and getting my money back was a nigh
reviews.text:
Bloomberg Digital charged me $399 instead of the $149 I agreed to — no warning, no consent. Apple’s investigation didn’t get my money back. Over an hour on the phone with Bloomberg support led to nothing but delays and a flat refund denial.
I checked the BBB and found many other customers reporting the same unexpected renewal charges and refund fights — this isn’t a one-off. Bloomberg L.P., founded by and still majority-owned by Michael Bloomberg, should be fixing this instead of making customers battle for money they never authorized.
I’m still demanding my $399 back. If you’re considering this subscription, check the BBB complaints first. I would not recommend it.

reviews.title: Laggy TV stream and embarrassing AI dictation — and you just broke the minimized video player
reviews.text:
I rely on Bloomberg TV during my workday, but the 1-minute lag in the TV stream makes this app useless when economic data releases or other events are happening in realtime.  

And the AI voice that reads news articles reminds me of automated market quotes from 20 years ago — it’s bad, like fingernails on a chalkboard.  Perplexing because The Economist, WaPo, and every other news app I use that has an AI dictation feature seem very natural.

Finally, the last update broke the video mini-player that’s supposed to shrink and overlay part of my screen when I need to look at something else in the app while watching (it still works properly when I multitask away to a different app).  The player also doesn’t change size when I rotate my phone anymore.  And I get BTV+ whether is select it in the settings or not — which is completely illegible on my small iPhone screen.  Amateur hour, guys.

Update: Now launching an article on the BBG stops my music from playing on Apple Music, for some reason — even though the article has no audio or video component.
